From the system developed, results were obtained based on the analysis of over 650 data points, indicating that when using only loop closure, the number of matching IDs for map creation ranges from 294 to 677. However, when TORO Optimizer is employed, the number of matching IDs becomes more limited, ranging from 182 to 538. The number of matching IDs decreases because TORO Optimizer removes some IDs deemed erroneous in the feature-matching process for map creation. From the results obtained, the TORO graph can reduce errors in loop closure, so making 3D area maps is better. It is hoped that by utilizing TORO Optimizer, the quality of 3D area mapping results can be enhanced for aerial mapping in search and rescue robot applications.

articleTitle: Reliability of Microclimate Data with IoT Technology on Coffee-Pine Farms in UB Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: The Coffee-Pine fields in UB Forest play a crucial role in the local ecosystem, with a microclimate that supports optimal plant growth. However, challenges to the reliability of microclimate data often arise, resulting in uncertainty in agricultural decision-making. This research focuses on the application of Internet of Things (IoT) technology to improve the accuracy and consistency of microclimate data. By installing IoT sensors at strategic points on the land, data is collected over a year. This research aims to analyze microclimate reliability data from two plots, LC and BAU. Microclimate data were evaluated based on data quality, including checking for missing data and outliers. Descriptive statistical analysis and data visualization were carried out to gain deeper insight into microclimate variations at both locations. The LC data showed missing data 13.92% for each parameter while the BAU data had little missing data. Both data sets show the presence of outliers. After cleaning, the data shows more consistent and realistic variations. Visual analysis shows fluctuations over time for all parameters, with some significant differences between LC and BAU. Microclimate data from LC and BAU show variations over time and between locations. Data quality is an important consideration in analysis, and data cleaning increases the reliability of results. The differences between LC and BAU are due to different location plots. This research confirms the potential of IoT technology in overcoming the problem of microclimate data reliability, providing a strong basis for sustainable agricultural practices on Coffee-Pine land in UB Forest.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Through Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease continues to be a significant cause of death in the modern world. Its strong connection with risk factors like smoking, high blood pressure, and elevated cholesterol levels highlights the importance of addressing these factors. This research aims to tackle the challenging task of predicting myocardial illness, a critical aspect of medical research. Accurate predictions are essential for improving healthcare strategies. In this study, we evaluate six different machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Bagging, XGBoost, and LightGBM. The results are promising, with accuracy rates as follows: Logistic Regression (81.00%), Support Vector Machine (75.01%), XGBoost (92.72%), LightGBM (90.60%), Decision Tree (82.30%), and Bagging (83.01%). Notably, XGBoost stands out as the best-performing model, highlighting its potential to enhance predictive accuracy for coronary infarction. As cardiovascular risk factors persist, incorporating advanced machine learning techniques has the potential to improve proactive medical interventions.

articleTitle: Chronic Disease Classification for Healthcare Facility Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Chronic diseases are a major cause of the global burden of disease, causing widespread death and disability worldwide. However, the underdevelopment of medical facilities in Indonesia has become a serious public health problem. A recommendation on the sequence of construction of health facilities using a chronic disease classification model is given and can be used by the government to allocate resources to build healthcare facilities in areas of greatest need to solve this problem. This study focuses on developing a chronic disease classification model using machine learning with a dataset from the Social Health Insurance Administration Body (BPJS). This dataset includes advanced referral facilities (FKRTL) data, non-capitation first-level facilities (FKTP) data, and membership data. The model will be used to make recommendations in order of health facility development. Research steps include data preprocessing, feature extraction, generation and evaluation of chronic disease classification models, and making recommendations on the development sequence of healthcare facilities. The testing scenarios were performed by comparing different models using test data, testing the confusion matrix as well as recall and f1-score to determine the best model. The results show that the decision tree model with feature selection has a recall of 98.127% and an f1-score of 86.776%, which is the best model to recommend on the order of development of medical facilities.

articleTitle: Using Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machines to Predict Television Channel Viewership
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: The proliferation of digital devices and the unprecedented growth in unstructured big data has rendered the dependence on traditional TV ratings practices obsolete. TV stations have to develop new ways of evaluating and predicting viewership, and this means analyzing the huge volumes of unstructured big data, mostly from the web and social media networks. One of those strategies is deploying machine learning algorithms. This study sought to analyze the performance of Naïve Bayes and SVM in predicting TV channel viewership, develop a hybrid model for predicting TV channel viewership, and determine whether a hybrid model has a higher predictive accuracy than Naïve Bayes and SVM. Based on two Twitter datasets for two competing TV shows (: NTV Kenya -AM Live and KTN Kenya - Morning Express), sentiment analysis revealed that the frequency of positive sentiments was 39.48% for AM Live and 39.41% for Morning Express. Similarly, negative sentiments, was also higher among AM Live audiences (19.03%) compared to Morning Express (14.60%). Neutral sentiments were higher among KTN Morning Express (41.98%) than AM Live (41.49%). Classification of viewer data in terms of tweet count, tweet replies, retweets, and likes revealed that KTN's Morning Express was the most popular show across all Twitter engagement metrics. On predictive accuracy, results showed that the hybrid algorithm had a higher predictive accuracy on the testing dataset (77%), compared to 65% for Naïve Bayes and 62% for SVM, thus demonstrating the value of hybrid algorithms in TV channel viewership prediction.

articleTitle: Emotion-Aware Fake News Detection on Social Media with BERT Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Fake news dissemination on social media poses a significant threat to the integrity of information and public discourse. This research proposes an emotion-aware fake news detection model using BERT embeddings. Leveraging the power of BERT, our model captures contextual relations in text, enabling accurate classification of fake news. Through experimentation with different BERT models, “bert-large-cased” emerges as the top-performing variant, achieving a remarkable training accuracy of 98% and an F1 score of 0.77. Integrating emotion-aware features enhances the model's efficacy in identifying fake news while minimizing false positives and negatives. Our study contributes to the field of fake news detection, offering a potent tool for safeguarding social media from disinformation.

articleTitle: Predicting Antiviral Compounds for Avian Influenza A/H9N2 Using Logistic Regression with RBF Kernel
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Avian Influenza A/H9N2 is a significant threat to the global poultry industry and presents occasional but severe health risks to humans. Given the potential ramifications of an outbreak, the swift and accurate identification of effective antiviral compounds becomes crucial. Traditional methods employed for predicting the efficacy of these compounds often encounter challenges, particularly in maintaining a balance between accuracy and efficiency. Recognizing these limitations, our study introduces an innovative predictive approach. We leverage the combined strengths of Radial Basis Function (RBF) networks and Logistic Regression. This methodology transforms compound features using the RBF network. The changed features are then fed into a Logistic Regression model to make predictions regarding efficacy. Initial findings from our research indicate a remarkable enhancement in prediction accuracy and precision compared to prevalent methods. Furthermore, our study provides a potentially transformative tool for antiviral compound prediction and establishes a precedent, emphasizing the profound potential of hybrid modeling techniques in advancing biomedical research.

articleTitle: Model-Based Learning Techniques for Accurate Heart Disease Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: The escalating global health crisis posed by cardiovascular disease, which claims an astonishing 17.9 million lives annually, necessitates precise and timely heart disease prediction, particularly in regions with limited access to advanced medical technology. Machine learning techniques have demonstrated potential in this regard, with previous studies achieving accuracies ranging from 86.6% to 90.78%. This paper addresses the urgency of accurate heart disease risk prediction by employing model-based learning techniques, focusing on four key algorithms: Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, and Random Forests. Leveraging the Heart Failure Prediction dataset, which we split into training and testing sets, we systematically evaluated the performance of these models. Our findings reveal that Support Vector Machine achieved an impressive accuracy of 90.76%, emphasizing its proficiency in classification. Gaussian Naive Bayes displayed a balanced performance with an accuracy of 88.59%, maintaining an equilibrium between precision and recall. Although Decision Tree exhibited slightly lower accuracy at 82.07%, it maintained a well-balanced trade-off. However, Random Forest stood out as the top performer, with an accuracy of 91.85%, excelling in classification, precision, and true positive detection. These results provide crucial guidance for selecting an optimal model, and future research avenues include hyperparameter fine-tuning, ensemble methods, larger datasets, and the interpretability of model predictions, particularly in the medical field, where accuracy and transparency are paramount. Overall, this study underscores the potential of model-based learning techniques in accurate heart disease prediction, with Random Forest emerging as a promising solution.

articleTitle: Enhancing Larval Classification Accuracy Through Hyperparameter Optimization in ResNet50 with Three Different Optimizers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Recent research has explored the application of deep learning models in the classification of Zophobas Morio and Tenebrio Molitor larvae, focusing on optimizing the choice of optimizer. This study aimed to investigate and compare the performance of the ResNet50 model using three different optimizers (Adam, Nadam, and Adagrad) for accurate classification of these larvae. We conducted an experimental study, training and evaluating the R model on a dataset of Zophobas Morio and Tenebrio Molitor larvae images using the mentioned optimizers. This study followed a quantitative approach to assess model performance. Our findings indicated that the Adam optimizer yielded the highest accuracy (approximately 97.1%), outperforming Nadam and Adagrad. However, recognizing Tenebrio Molitor still presented challenges, highlighting room for improvement. The results suggest that the choice of optimizer significantly influences the model's performance in larva classification. While Adam showed promising results, further enhancements are needed for accurate Tenebrio Molitor recognition. Future research should explore different deep learning architectures and larger datasets for improved classification outcomes.

articleTitle: Welcome Speech
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: My respects, plenary speakers and participants of the ICMERALDA: International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning, And Digital Applications. I am pleased to welcome you all to The First International Conference ICMERALDA, the new International Conference we are holding in 2023 (two thousand and twenty-three). We are grateful that in holding this conference, there were so many participants, even more than what we targeted, and the participants came from several countries, which we note here are more than 16 (sixteen) countries.

articleTitle: Foreword
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling & E-Information Research, Artificial Learning and Digital Applications (ICMERALDA)
abstract: Nowadays, our way of life is experiencing a rise of intelligent technology that can shape how we interact, from artificial intelligence, robotics, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Digital transformation has appeared in exploring sophistication in several fields that utilize machines at the front lines of the Smart Technology Revolution. Artificial intelligence allows systems to learn and improve experience without explicit programming. It contributes to the significance of more effective and efficient research breakthroughs in the future. A network of devices that are interconnected and communicate with each other can optimize the production process and smooth tasks in various aspects of our daily lives.
